question: Who is the author of the Indian national anthem?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rabindranath Tagore composed "Jana Gana Mana", which was adopted as the National Anthem of India by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950. (राष्ट्रगान — रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर)

 

• It was originally composed in Bengali and was first sung at the Calcutta Session of the Indian National Congress on 27 December 1911.

 

• Tagore was also the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913), for his collection "Gitanjali".

 

• The full song has five stanzas; only the first stanza is the official National Anthem, and it takes about 52 seconds to sing in full.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rabindranath Tagore also wrote "Amar Shonar Bangla", the national anthem of Bangladesh, and is said to have inspired Sri Lanka's national anthem as well.

 

• India's National Song, "Vande Mataram", was written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in his novel Anandmath.

 

NOTE

 

• Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay (Option 1): He wrote "Vande Mataram", India's National Song, not the National Anthem.

 

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (Option 2): A 19th-century social reformer and educationist, not associated with the national anthem.

 

• Kazi Nazrul Islam (Option 3): Known as the "Rebel Poet" (Bidrohi Kobi) and Bangladesh's national poet; he did not write India's national anthem.

question: Which MS Excel function can be used to sum up the numbers entered in a group of cells?
solution_text:
The correct answer is SUM.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The SUM function in MS Excel adds up all the numbers in a selected range of cells, e.g. `=SUM(A1:A10)`. (योग फलन — SUM)

 

• It is one of the most frequently used Excel functions and can take individual cell references, ranges, or a mix of both as arguments.

 

• SUM automatically ignores text and empty cells within the selected range, adding only numeric values.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Related functions include SUMIF (sums values meeting one condition) and SUMIFS (sums values meeting multiple conditions).

 

• The AutoSum button (Σ) on the Home tab is a shortcut that automatically inserts the SUM function.

 

NOTE

 

• COUNT (Option 1): Counts the number of cells that contain numeric values; it does not add them.

 

• AVERAGE (Option 2): Calculates the arithmetic mean of the numbers in a range.

 

• MAX (Option 3): Returns the largest value among the selected numbers.

question: Which of the Mendel's laws states that a diploid organism passes a randomly selected allele for a trait to its offspring, such that the offspring inherit one allele from each parent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Law of segregation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mendel's Law of Segregation states that each organism carries two alleles for a trait, and these alleles separate (segregate) randomly during gamete formation, so each gamete carries only one allele. (पृथक्करण का नियम — मेंडल का द्वितीय नियम)

 

• As a result, the offspring receives one allele from each parent, restoring the paired condition at fertilisation.

 

• This law is also known as Mendel's Second Law and is based on his monohybrid cross experiments with pea plants (Pisum sativum).

 

• It explains why traits controlled by a single gene can reappear in later generations even if masked in a parent (e.g., in the F2 generation of a monohybrid cross).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mendel's Law of Dominance states that in a heterozygous pair, one allele (dominant) masks the expression of the other (recessive).

 

• Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment (Third Law) states that alleles of different genes assort independently of one another during gamete formation, based on his dihybrid cross experiments.

 

NOTE

 

• Law of dominance (Option 1): Concerns which of two alleles is expressed in a heterozygote, not how alleles segregate into gametes.

 

• Law of paired factor (Option 2): Not one of Mendel's three named laws; alleles occurring in pairs is an underlying principle, not this specific law.

 

• Law of independent assortment (Option 3): Governs the inheritance of two or more traits simultaneously (genes on different chromosomes), not the segregation of a single pair of alleles.

question: In 2026, which country will host Asian Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Japan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2026 Asian Games (20th edition) will be hosted by Nagoya, in Aichi Prefecture, Japan. (एशियाई खेल 2026 — जापान)

 

• This will be the third time Japan hosts the Asian Games, after Tokyo (1958) and Hiroshima (1994).

 

• The event is organised under the aegis of the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2023 Asian Games (19th edition) were held in Hangzhou, China.

 

• The 2030 Asian Games are scheduled to be hosted by Doha, Qatar, and the 2034 edition by Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

 

NOTE

 

• India (Option 1): India last hosted the Asian Games in 1982 (New Delhi) and is not the host for 2026.

 

• China (Option 2): China hosted the most recent (2023) edition in Hangzhou, not the 2026 edition.

 

• Nepal (Option 4): Nepal has never hosted the Asian Games.

question: Which directive principle has been implemented in establishing Handloom and Handicrafts Boards?
option_1: Promote cottage industries on cooperative basis
option_2: Provision for just and humane condition of work
option_3: Participation of workers in management of Industries
solution_text:
The correct answer is Promote cottage industries on cooperative basis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 43 of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) directs the State to endeavour to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas. (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व — अनुच्छेद 43)

 

• Bodies like the All India Handloom Board and All India Handicrafts Board were set up to give effect to this directive by supporting artisans and cottage/village industries.

 

• DPSPs, contained in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Constitution, are non-justiciable but fundamental in the governance of the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 43 was later supplemented by Article 43B (added by the 97th Amendment, 2011), which promotes co-operative societies.

 

• DPSPs are inspired by the Irish Constitution and aim to establish a welfare state and social/economic democracy.

 

NOTE

 

• Provision for just and humane condition of work (Option 2): This is covered under Article 42, relating to work conditions and maternity relief.

 

• Participation of workers in management of Industries (Option 3): This is covered under Article 43A, added by the 42nd Amendment (1976).

 

• Protection and improvement of environment (Option 4): This is covered under Article 48A, also added by the 42nd Amendment (1976).

question: Give Plastic and Take Gold scheme was launched in the village of which State/UT in year 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jammu and Kashmir.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The "Give Plastic and Take Gold" initiative was launched in April 2023 in Sadiwara village, Anantnag district, South Kashmir, Jammu and Kashmir. (प्लास्टिक दो, सोना लो — जम्मू और कश्मीर)

 

• Under the scheme, villagers who collected 20 quintals of plastic waste were rewarded with a gold coin, an idea started by the village Sarpanch.

 

• The initiative successfully made the entire village plastic-free within about 15 days of its launch, drawing wide attention as a grassroots environmental model.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The scheme is an example of a community-driven Swachh Bharat-style initiative aimed at plastic waste management at the village/panchayat level.

 

• Similar plastic-collection-for-reward drives have since been replicated in other parts of India to promote a plastic-free environment.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 1): Not the location of this scheme.

 

• Lakshadweep (Option 2): Not the location of this scheme.

 

• Assam (Option 4): Not the location of this scheme.

question: Marathi language is in the _______ language family.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indo Aryan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Marathi belongs to the Indo-Aryan branch of the Indo-European language family, and is the official language of Maharashtra. (मराठी भाषा — भारोपीय भाषा परिवार)

 

• It evolved from Maharashtri Prakrit, an ancient Prakrit language, and is written in the Devanagari script.

 

• Marathi is one of the 22 scheduled languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution and was given Classical Language status by the Government of India in 2024.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major Indo-Aryan languages include Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati, Punjabi, and Odia.

 

• Austroasiatic (Austric) languages in India include Santhali and Mundari, spoken mainly by tribal communities in eastern and central India.

 

NOTE

 

• Austro (Option 1): Not a recognised standalone language family classification for Marathi.

 

• Sino-India (Option 2): Not a valid language family name; the Sino-Tibetan family covers languages like Bodo and Manipuri, not Marathi.

 

• Austric (Option 3): Refers to the Austroasiatic family (e.g., Santhali, Khasi), unrelated to Marathi.

question: The music of traditional _______ consists of thumri and other lyrical song forms.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kathak, a classical dance form of North India, uses thumri and other light, lyrical semi-classical song forms (along with dadra, ghazal, and bhajan) to accompany its expressive (abhinaya) portions. (कथक — ठुमरी)

 

• Kathak originated from storytelling traditions of kathakars (storytellers) and later developed distinct Jaipur, Lucknow, and Banaras gharanas.

 

• It is characterised by intricate footwork (tatkar), fast spins (chakkars), and subtle facial/hand expressions used to portray thumri's romantic and devotional themes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Thumri itself is a semi-classical vocal genre that emerged in Lucknow in the 19th century, dealing mainly with themes of love, particularly Radha-Krishna devotion.

 

• India's eight recognised classical dance forms are Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya.

 

NOTE

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 1): A classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, traditionally accompanied by Carnatic music, not thumri.

 

• Kathakali (Option 3): A classical dance-drama of Kerala, using Carnatic-style vocal music (sopanam), not thumri.

 

• Sattriya (Option 4): A classical dance form of Assam, originating in Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras), accompanied by borgeet music, not thumri.

question: Gandhi Jayanti marks the birthday of the father of the nation Mahatma Gandhi, who was born at __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Porbandar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahatma Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 in Porbandar, a coastal town in present-day Gujarat. (महात्मा गांधी — पोरबंदर)

 

• Gandhi Jayanti, observed every year on 2 October, is a national holiday commemorating his birth and is also observed internationally as the International Day of Non-Violence.

 

• Gandhi's birthplace, Kirti Mandir, in Porbandar is preserved as a memorial and is a popular heritage site.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi is popularly known as the "Father of the Nation"; the title was first used for him by Subhas Chandra Bose in a 1944 radio broadcast.

 

• Gandhi studied law in London and began his activism in South Africa before returning to India in 1915 to lead the freedom struggle.

 

NOTE

 

• Ahmedabad (Option 1): Site of the Sabarmati Ashram, from where Gandhi led the Dandi March (1930), but not his birthplace.

 

• Vadodara (Option 2): A major city in Gujarat, but not associated with Gandhi's birth.

 

• Gandhinagar (Option 4): The capital of Gujarat, named in Gandhi's honour, but not his birthplace.

question: Ohira folk music is primarily associated with one of the popular festivals of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ohira folk music is closely linked to the tribal cultural heritage of Jharkhand and is performed during its major community festivals. (ओहिरा लोकगीत — झारखंड)

 

• Jharkhand celebrates several important tribal festivals such as Sarhul, Karma, and Sohrai, where traditional folk music and dance play a central role in community celebration.

 

• Ohira, like other Jharkhandi folk traditions such as Jhumar and Domkach, reflects the state's rich tribal (Adivasi) musical heritage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Karma festival of Jharkhand is dedicated to the worship of the Karam tree/deity for prosperity and a good harvest.

 

• Other well-known folk dance forms of Jharkhand include Chhau, Paika, and Domkach.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 1): Known for folk forms like Theyyam and Padayani, not Ohira.

 

• Assam (Option 2): Known for Bihu songs and dance, not Ohira.

 

• Karnataka (Option 4): Known for folk forms like Yakshagana and Dollu Kunitha, not Ohira.

question: Which of the following planets' atmosphere is made up of thick white and yellowish clouds of sulphuric acid?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Venus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Venus's atmosphere is composed mainly of carbon dioxide and is covered in thick, opaque white and yellowish clouds of sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄). (शुक्र ग्रह — सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल के बादल)

 

• These dense clouds reflect sunlight strongly, making Venus the brightest planet as seen from Earth, and trap heat, causing a runaway greenhouse effect.

 

• As a result, Venus has a surface temperature of around 465°C, making it the hottest planet in the solar system, even hotter than Mercury.

 

• Venus is also known as Earth's "sister planet" because of its similar size and mass, and it rotates in a retrograde (east-to-west) direction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Venus has extremely high atmospheric pressure at its surface, about 92 times that of Earth.

 

• Venus has no natural satellites (moons), similar to Mercury.

 

NOTE

 

• Neptune (Option 2): Its blue colour comes from methane in its hydrogen-helium atmosphere, not sulphuric acid clouds.

 

• Mars (Option 3): Has a thin atmosphere composed mostly of carbon dioxide, without sulphuric acid clouds.

 

• Jupiter (Option 4): Its atmosphere is mainly hydrogen and helium, with bands of ammonia-based clouds, not sulphuric acid.

question: Which of the following is a public sector owned and operated entity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is BHEL.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• BHEL (Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited) is a Maharatna Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE), owned and operated by the Government of India under the Ministry of Heavy Industries. (भारत हेवी इलेक्ट्रिकल्स लिमिटेड — सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र)

 

• Incorporated in 1964, BHEL is India's largest engineering and manufacturing company engaged in power generation equipment, transmission, industrial, and defence products.

 

• It has manufacturing units across the country, including at Bhopal, Haridwar, Hyderabad, and Tiruchirappalli.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• BHEL contributes a significant share of India's total installed power generation capacity through its equipment.

 

• India's Central Public Sector Enterprises are graded as Maharatna, Navratna, and Miniratna based on financial strength and operational autonomy.

 

NOTE

 

• Bajaj Auto Ltd (Option 1): A private-sector automobile manufacturer, part of the Bajaj Group, not government-owned.

 

• Oil India Ltd. (Option 2): Also a government-owned Navratna PSU; however, per the officially marked key for this question, BHEL is treated as the intended answer.

 

• Tata Steel Ltd (Option 4): A private-sector company belonging to the Tata Group, not government-owned.

question: According to Census of India 2011, which district in India has the lowest literacy rate in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alirajpur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, Alirajpur district in Madhya Pradesh recorded the lowest literacy rate in India, at around 37%. (अलीराजपुर जिला — न्यूनतम साक्षरता दर)

 

• Alirajpur is a predominantly tribal district (largely Bhil and Bhilala communities), which is one of the key factors behind its low literacy figures.

 

• Alirajpur was carved out of Jhabua district in Madhya Pradesh in 2008.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate among Indian states (over 93%), while Bihar recorded the lowest among states.

 

• India's overall literacy rate as per Census 2011 was about 74.04% (male: ~82.14%, female: ~65.46%).

 

NOTE

 

• Rampur (Option 1): A district in Uttar Pradesh; not the lowest-literacy district nationally.

 

• Madhubani (Option 2): A district in Bihar with relatively low literacy, but not the lowest in India.

 

• Aizwal (Option 4): Aizawl, the capital district of Mizoram, in fact has one of the highest literacy rates in India, not the lowest.

question: The Tokyo Paralympics 2020 gold medal winner Krishna Nagar is associated with _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is badminton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Krishna Nagar won the gold medal in the men's singles SH6 badminton event at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics (held in 2021). (कृष्णा नागर — बैडमिंटन)

 

• He defeated Hong Kong's Chu Man Kai in the final to claim India's second gold medal in badminton at that edition of the Paralympics.

 

• The SH6 category is for para-athletes with short stature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• At Tokyo 2020, Pramod Bhagat also won gold in the men's singles SL3 badminton category, India's first-ever Paralympic badminton gold.

 

• India's overall best-ever Paralympic performance came at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, where the contingent won 29 medals.

 

NOTE

 

• Shooting (Option 1): India's notable Paralympic shooters include Avani Lekhara, not Krishna Nagar.

 

• Wrestling (Option 2): Not Krishna Nagar's sport; wrestling is not currently a Paralympic sport.

 

• Table tennis (Option 3): India's notable Paralympic table tennis players include Bhavina Patel, not Krishna Nagar.

question: Which is the Standard Meridian of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 82°30ʹ E.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Standard Meridian of India is 82°30' E longitude, which is used to calculate Indian Standard Time (IST). (भारतीय मानक याम्योत्तर — 82°30' पूर्व)

 

• This meridian passes through Mirzapur, in Uttar Pradesh, near Allahabad (Prayagraj), which is treated as the reference location for IST.

 

• IST is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT/UTC), and applies uniformly across the whole country despite its east-west longitudinal spread.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's total longitudinal extent is from about 68°7' E to 97°25' E, spanning roughly 29 degrees of longitude.

 

• The Standard Meridian was adopted in 1906, and the entire country follows a single time zone based on it (with occasional proposals for a second time zone for the northeast).

 

NOTE

 

• 84°40' E (Option 1): Not India's Standard Meridian.

 

• 81°30' E (Option 3): Close to but not the actual Standard Meridian value.

 

• 83°30' E (Option 4): Close to but not the actual Standard Meridian value.

question: Who is Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission as on 31 March 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shri Manoj Soni.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Manoj Soni was serving as the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) as of 31 March 2024, having taken charge in May 2023. (संघ लोक सेवा आयोग अध्यक्ष — मनोज सोनी)

 

• The UPSC is a constitutional body established under Article 315 of the Constitution of India, responsible for recruitment to All India Services and Central Civil Services.

 

• Dr. Manoj Soni resigned from the post in July 2024, before completing his term.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The UPSC Chairman and members are appointed by the President of India and can hold office until the age of 65 years or a term of six years, whichever is earlier.

 

• Provisions relating to UPSC are covered under Articles 315 to 323 of the Indian Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Mrs. Preeti Sudan (Option 1): A former Union Health Secretary; she was not UPSC Chairman as of the date in question.

 

• Shri BN Jha (Option 3): Not the UPSC Chairman as of 31 March 2024.

 

• Ms. Smita Nagaraj (Option 4): A UPSC member at the time, but not the Chairman.

question: The process of merging data from a data source into a main document in a word-processing application is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is mail merge.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mail merge is a feature in word-processing applications (such as MS Word) that combines data from a data source (e.g., an Excel sheet or address list) with a main document template to automatically generate multiple personalised documents. (मेल मर्ज — डेटा स्रोत और मुख्य दस्तावेज़)

 

• It is commonly used to create personalised letters, envelopes, labels, and emails for a large number of recipients from a single template.

 

• The process typically involves selecting a main document, connecting a data source, inserting merge fields, and then completing the merge to produce individual outputs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• In MS Word, mail merge is accessed via the "Mailings" tab, using the "Start Mail Merge" wizard.

 

• Common data sources for mail merge include Excel spreadsheets, Access databases, and Outlook contact lists.

 

NOTE

 

• Data concatenation (Option 1): Refers to joining two or more strings/values together, not merging documents with a data source.

 

• Data accumulation (Option 3): Not a standard word-processing term for this feature.

 

• Data integration (Option 4): A broader IT term for combining data from different sources into a unified view, not specific to word-processing document generation.

question: In 1960, which isotope was used to define the standard measure of length?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Krypton-86.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1960, the General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM) redefined the metre in terms of the wavelength of light emitted by the Krypton-86 isotope, specifically 1,650,763.73 wavelengths of the orange-red spectral line of Krypton-86 in a vacuum. (क्रिप्टॉन-86 — मीटर की परिभाषा, 1960)

 

• This replaced the earlier definition based on the International Prototype Metre, a physical platinum-iridium bar kept in France.

 

• The Krypton-86-based definition was itself later replaced in 1983, when the metre was redefined in terms of the speed of light in vacuum.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The current (1983) definition: 1 metre = distance travelled by light in vacuum in 1/299,792,458 of a second.

 

• The SI unit system is maintained by the International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM), based in Sèvres, France.

 

NOTE

 

• Krypton-88 (Option 2): Not the isotope used for the 1960 metre definition.

 

• Krypton-83 (Option 3): Not the isotope used for the 1960 metre definition.

 

• Krypton-90 (Option 4): Not the isotope used for the 1960 metre definition.

question: Who is the Union Minister of Civil Aviation in Government of India? (As of March, 2024).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jyotiraditya M. Scindia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jyotiraditya M. Scindia was serving as the Union Minister of Civil Aviation (as well as Steel) in the Government of India as of March 2024, during the second Modi government (2021-2024). (नागरिक उड्डयन मंत्री — ज्योतिरादित्य सिंधिया)

 

• The Ministry of Civil Aviation is responsible for formulation of national civil aviation policy, regulation of air transport, and safety/security of aircraft operations in India.

 

• Scindia continued to hold the Civil Aviation portfolio after the formation of the third Modi government in June 2024.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Key initiatives under his tenure included the expansion of the UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik) regional connectivity scheme and airport infrastructure growth.

 

• The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is the regulatory body governing civil aviation safety in India.

 

NOTE

 

• G Kishan Reddy (Option 1): Held the Union Ministry of Coal and Mines, and earlier Tourism and Culture, not Civil Aviation.

 

• Kiren Rijiju (Option 2): Held portfolios such as Law and Justice, and Earth Sciences, not Civil Aviation.

 

• Raj Kumar Singh (Option 3): Held the Union Ministry of Power and New & Renewable Energy, not Civil Aviation.

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a monopoly?
option_2: Full control over the price by the seller
solution_text:
The correct answer is One buyer and many sellers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A monopoly is a market structure characterised by a single seller facing many buyers — the exact opposite of "one buyer and many sellers". (एकाधिकार — एक विक्रेता, अनेक क्रेता)

 

• "One buyer and many sellers" actually describes a monopsony, not a monopoly, so it is NOT a feature of monopoly.

 

• Genuine features of monopoly include a single seller controlling the entire market supply, no close substitutes for the product, and significant barriers to entry for new firms.

 

• Because there is only one seller, that seller has considerable control over the price it charges (a "price maker"), unlike firms in perfectly competitive markets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Market structures in economics are broadly classified as perfect competition, monopolistic competition, oligopoly, and monopoly, based on the number of buyers/sellers and product differentiation.

 

• A market with one buyer and many sellers (monopsony) is seen, for example, in some government procurement or single-employer labour markets.

 

NOTE

 

• No close substitutes (Option 1): This IS a genuine feature of monopoly, so it is incorrectly excluded here — the question asks which is NOT a feature.

 

• Full control over the price by the seller (Option 2): This IS a genuine feature of monopoly.

 

• One seller and many buyers (Option 4): This IS the defining feature of monopoly, not something excluded from it.

question: There is a cable manufacturing facility at HCL in Rupnarainpur. It is belong to which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hindustan Cables Limited (HCL), a public sector undertaking, has its main cable manufacturing facility at Rupnarayanpur, located in the Paschim Bardhaman district of West Bengal. (रूपनारायणपुर — पश्चिम बंगाल)

 

• Hindustan Cables Limited was set up in 1952 as India's first telecommunication cable manufacturing company, under the Department of Telecommunications.

 

• Rupnarayanpur, on the banks of the river Barakar, developed as an industrial township around this HCL unit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• West Bengal is also home to other major industrial hubs like Durgapur (steel) and Haldia (petrochemicals/port).

 

• HCL (Hindustan Cables Limited) should not be confused with the private IT company HCL Technologies.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam (Option 1): Not the location of this HCL cable facility.

 

• Haryana (Option 2): Not the location of this HCL cable facility.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): Not the location of this HCL cable facility.

question: Due to the efforts of whom among the following social reformers was the first Hindu Widow Remarriage Act introduced and passed in 1856?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, a prominent Bengali social reformer and educationist, campaigned tirelessly for the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856, which legalised the remarriage of Hindu widows. (हिंदू विधवा पुनर्विवाह अधिनियम 1856 — ईश्वर चंद्र विद्यासागर)

 

• The Act was passed during the tenure of Governor-General Lord Canning, largely due to Vidyasagar's persistent advocacy and petitions.

 

• Vidyasagar was also a key figure in promoting women's education and opposed practices like child marriage and polygamy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vidyasagar reformed the Bengali alphabet and simplified Bengali prose writing, and served as the principal of Sanskrit College, Calcutta.

 

• He is also remembered for his contributions to setting up schools for girls across Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Radhakant Deb (Option 1): A conservative Hindu leader who actually opposed widow remarriage and other reformist measures of that era.

 

• Atmaram Pandurang (Option 2): Founder of the Prarthana Samaj (1867) in Bombay, a later reform movement, not associated with the 1856 Act.

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Option 4): A pioneering reformer known for the abolition of Sati (1829), but he died in 1833, before the 1856 Widow Remarriage Act.

question: Who among the following was the first Sultan of Delhi to style himself as 'Zil-i-Ilahi'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Balban.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ghiyasuddin Balban, a ruler of the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, was the first Sultan of Delhi to style himself as "Zil-i-Ilahi" (Shadow of God on Earth). (ज़िल-ए-इलाही — बलबन)

 

• Balban strongly emphasised the theory of kingship and divine right to rule, introducing strict court etiquette such as sijda (prostration) and paibos (kissing the monarch's feet).

 

• He also established a rigorous military and administrative system, including the "Blood and Iron" policy, to consolidate central authority and suppress rebellious nobles (the "Chalisa" or Forty).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Balban ruled from 1266 to 1287 CE and was a former slave (Turkic) who rose through the ranks under Iltutmish.

 

• He is also credited with reorganising the Diwan-i-Arz (military department) to strengthen the army.

 

NOTE

 

• Qutbuddin Aibak (Option 1): Founder of the Slave Dynasty (1206), who began construction of the Qutub Minar; he did not use the title Zil-i-Ilahi.

 

• Feroz Shah (Option 2): Refers to a Tughlaq-era ruler (Firoz Shah Tughlaq); not the first to adopt this title.

 

• Iltutmish (Option 4): Consolidated the Delhi Sultanate and introduced the Iqta system and silver Tanka, but he was not the first to style himself Zil-i-Ilahi.

question: The Constitution of India was adopted on ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 26 November 1949.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constituent Assembly of India formally adopted the Constitution of India on 26 November 1949; it came into force on 26 January 1950. (संविधान अंगीकरण — 26 नवंबर 1949)

 

• 26 November is now observed every year as "Samvidhan Diwas" (Constitution Day) in India.

 

• The Constitution was drafted by the Drafting Committee, chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, and took about 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to complete.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• 26 January was chosen as the date of commencement to commemorate the "Purna Swaraj" (complete independence) declaration made by the Indian National Congress on 26 January 1930.

 

• The original Constitution had 395 Articles, 22 Parts, and 8 Schedules; it has since been amended many times and now has 12 Schedules.

 

NOTE

 

• 24 November 1947 (Option 2): Incorrect date; the Constituent Assembly's work was still ongoing at this time.

 

• 26 January 1949 (Option 3): Incorrect date and year combination for adoption.

 

• 26 January 1950 (Option 4): This is the date the Constitution came into force, not the date it was adopted.

question: Who was the first Indian wrestler to win Gold at the World Championships in 2010?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sushil Kumar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sushil Kumar became the first Indian wrestler to win a gold medal at the World Wrestling Championships, held in Moscow, Russia, in 2010, in the 66 kg freestyle category. (सुशील कुमार — विश्व कुश्ती चैंपियनशिप 2010)

 

• He had earlier won a bronze medal at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, and went on to win a silver medal at the 2012 London Olympics, both in freestyle wrestling.

 

• Sushil Kumar has been honoured with the Khel Ratna Award and Padma Shri, among other honours, for his contributions to Indian wrestling.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other prominent freestyle wrestlers include Bajrang Punia (World Championship medals, Tokyo Olympics bronze) and Yogeshwar Dutt (2012 London Olympics bronze).

 

• In women's wrestling, Vinesh Phogat and Sakshi Malik (2016 Rio Olympics bronze) are notable Indian achievers.

 

NOTE

 

• Alka Tomar (Option 1): An accomplished Indian woman wrestler with Asian and Commonwealth medals, but not the first Indian gold medallist at the World Championships.

 

• Bajrang Punia (Option 3): A leading Indian wrestler with World Championship medals (silver/bronze) in later years, but not the first Indian gold medallist there.

 

• Geeta Phogat (Option 4): Known for being India's first female wrestler to win a Commonwealth Games gold (2010), not a World Championship gold.
